pieces.title: Game shell and screens
pieces.what: Make the page load a canvas, a title screen and a game-over screen with restart, driven by a small state machine. No tank or wall code yet, but the game must run.

pieces.title: Two tanks and split screen
pieces.what: Two tanks with keyboard controls, each drawn in its own half of a split screen with a divider. Movement and turret aiming only; no bullets or walls.

pieces.title: Shooting and bullets
pieces.what: Each tank fires bullets that bounce once off the arena edge and kill the other tank on hit, awarding a point and restarting the round. Must not add power-ups or destructible walls.

pieces.title: Destructible walls
pieces.what: Generate a wall layout for the arena; bullets carve or destroy wall tiles on impact. Must not change tank movement or bullets' damage.

pieces.title: Power-ups
pieces.what: Spawn power-ups in the arena that a tank picks up by driving over, granting a temporary speed, shield or triple-shot. Must not alter wall or split-screen code.

pieces.title: Sound and polish
pieces.what: Add firing, hit, pickup and round-end sounds with on/off toggle, plus a score display at the top of each screen. Must not change gameplay numbers, only read them.

summary: A two-player tank game on one keyboard, split screen so each player sees their own tank, with walls that can be shot away and power-ups that give a temporary edge. Rounds end when a tank is destroyed and the winner scores a point.
assumptions: Both players share one keyboard: player one uses WASD plus a fire key, player two uses the arrow keys plus a fire key.
Split screen is horizontal: player one on top, player two underneath, so both see the same arena from the same top-down view.
The arena is a fixed size that fits the screen, not a scrolling world.
Bullets kill in one hit, and there are no lives or respawns within a round.
Walls are destroyed in tiles by bullet hits rather than cracking in stages.
Power-ups are temporary and last a fixed number of seconds.
Scores are shown but there is no match-length win condition yet; play continues until the players stop.
